key_insight: Pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials can efficiently capture how oxygen-related defects suppress thermal transport in AlN, including defect complexes and non-dilute scattering effects.
engineering_relevance: The approach provides a practical route to predict and tune thermal conductivity in AlN thermal-management materials under realistic impurity conditions.
method: Benchmark several pretrained MLIPs against DFT for phonons and pristine thermal conductivity
Use a fine-tuned SevenNet-Nano model in molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo annealing to form defect complexes
Extract defect scattering from SED linewidths and feed it into iterative BTE calculations
evidence_signal: The defect scattering rates and thermal conductivities were compared against harmonic T-matrix predictions and experimental trends, with good agreement at low oxygen content and realistic conductivity decrease with increasing oxygen.
watch_item: At higher defect concentrations, scattering no longer scales linearly with oxygen content, so dilute independent-defect assumptions and pristine-phonon models can break down.
paper_title: Defect-limited thermal transport in AlN using pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials
